quote.text: Because I have no natural gifts, shall I on that account give up my discipline? Far be it from me! Epictetus will not be better than Socrates, but if only I am not worse, that suffices me. For I shall not be a Milo, either, and yet I do not neglect my body, nor a Croesus, and yet I do not neglect my property, nor, in a word, is there any other field in which we give up the appropriate discipline merely from despair of attaining the highest.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Even if one feels lacking in innate talents, disciplined consistency in nurturing children sets a firm foundation for their growth.
    • By modeling perseverance through small, regular acts of care and guidance, you show your children that steady effort is as valuable as any natural gift.
  • Leadership
    • True leadership is forged through disciplined effort rather than relying solely on natural charisma or talent.
    • Embrace a mindset of constant improvement; by leading with integrity and discipline, you inspire your team to pursue excellence regardless of their starting point.
  • Product Management
    • Like any challenging endeavor, successful product management demands structured discipline—even if breakthroughs do not come immediately.
    • Focus on incremental progress, systematic learning, and consistent execution, knowing that perseverance shapes success more reliably than raw, innate ability.
